title: env_manifest
description: Machine-readable, git-tracked fact file for a generated verification environment: env.manifest.json. It has exactly three top-level layers -- vip_config (the VIP's own already-resolved config object, dumped by a zero-time UVM callback at end_of_elaboration_phase -- more reliable than a user guide because it reflects actually-applied values), dut_facts (ports/params reverse-derived from real verible --export_json RTL parsing, plus registers from a structured RAL/IP-XACT-style source), and env_topology (component hierarchy + config_db set/get pairing captured from a real uvm_top.print_topology() + +UVM_CONFIG_DB_TRACE run). Generated only -- dv_harness/env_manifest.py is the sole writer; this file is never hand-edited. Every layer that requires a real captured artifact (a VIP config dump, a topology dump, a config_db trace log) reports status=NOT_AVAILABLE with a `reason` when that artifact does not yet exist, rather than fabricating example content -- an agent reading this file must be able to tell 'genuinely captured from a real run' apart from 'not yet captured' at a glance. Deterministic key ordering and no timestamp/nondeterministic fields are baked into the content itself, so re-running the generator against unchanged real inputs produces a byte-identical file (a real diff means a real underlying change) -- this is why the schema deliberately has no 'generated_at'-style field. Schema 1.2 (2026-09-06) narrows that contract deliberately and honestly: `generator` now carries spec section 210's per-artifact generation provenance tuple, including the real harness git SHA, so a manifest regenerated after the HARNESS ITSELF moved to a new commit differs in generator.repository_sha.harness -- which is a real underlying change (a different generator produced the artifact), not clock noise. Unchanged inputs AND an unchanged harness commit still produce a byte-identical file.

generator.description: Spec section 210's per-artifact GENERATION PROVENANCE TUPLE: which TOOL, at which TOOL VERSION and SCHEMA VERSION, driven by WHICH INPUT, produced by WHICH AGENT/SKILL, from WHICH COMMIT. Added in schema 1.2 (2026-09-06) INSIDE this existing block rather than as a second provenance record beside it. Every sub-object always carries every key with an explicit status, so 'this was not declared' and 'this key was omitted' can never look alike. Nothing here is ever fabricated: an undeclared agent is NOT_DECLARED, a declared identifier matching no real profile is DECLARED with resolution NOT_FOUND, and an unresolvable git HEAD is NOT_AVAILABLE with its real reason.

version.description: env_manifest.py's own SCHEMA_VERSION at generation time, not a build timestamp -- kept diffable. This is the SCHEMA's version; the harness build that produced the file is tool_version below. Before schema 1.2 there was no such field, so 'which harness produced this' was answerable only by misreading this one.

tool_version.description: The real dv_harness package version (dv_harness.__version__) at generation time, e.g. '15.0.0'. Deliberately distinct from `version` above.

agent.description: Which agent or skill produced this artifact, in the convention the profiles themselves use to self-identify: the YAML front-matter `name:` of a .claude/agents/*.md profile or a .claude/skills/**/SKILL.md skill. A declared identifier is CHECKED against the real profiles on disk by env_manifest.known_generation_identifiers().

status.description: DECLARED: the caller named a producing agent/skill. NOT_DECLARED: nobody claimed authorship -- recorded honestly rather than attributed to a default.

identifier.description: The declared profile name verbatim; null when NOT_DECLARED. Never invented.

resolution.description: AGENT_PROFILE/SKILL: a real profile in this checkout really declares this name. NOT_FOUND: a name was declared and no profile carries it -- recorded as declared, never accepted as verified. PROFILE_TREE_NOT_AVAILABLE: no .claude tree beside this harness, so nobody could check -- deliberately distinct from NOT_FOUND.

input_ir.description: What drove this generation. Two declared forms: a section 184 requirement CONTRACT (kind=requirement_contract), located in a real requirements document and cross-checked through requirement_contract.validate_requirement_contract() and downstream_consumable() -- so a manifest that cites a requirement also records whether that requirement was actually fit to generate from, rather than merely naming it; or a plain input FILE (kind=file) recorded as path + real sha256 + byte size, never content.

status.description: RESOLVED: the declared input really exists and (for a contract) really validates. NOT_FOUND: declared but absent or unlocatable. INVALID: located but not a schema-valid requirement contract. NOT_DECLARED: nobody named an input.

reference.description: The requirement_id (contract form) or the declared file path (file form).

contract_schema_version.description: The cited requirement record's own contract_schema_version; null for the file form.

requirement_status.description: The cited requirement's own five-value status (COMPLETE/PARTIAL/AMBIGUOUS/CONTRADICTORY/UNKNOWN); null for the file form.

downstream_consumable.description: requirement_contract.downstream_consumable()'s real verdict on the cited requirement -- whether a generator was entitled to build from it at all. Null for the file form and whenever the record did not validate.

repository_sha.description: The real current git SHA(s) this artifact was generated at, read by the EXISTING change_impact.resolve_sha() (a real `git rev-parse --verify HEAD^{commit}`) -- there is no second git reader in this package. No absolute repository path is recorded, so the manifest stays diffable across machines.

harness.description: HEAD of the checkout containing dv_harness/env_manifest.py -- the GENERATOR's own identity. Always attempted, and always read from this file's own location rather than from a caller-supplied path, so it cannot be pointed at a different repository.

project.description: HEAD of the project root this manifest belongs to. NOT_DECLARED unless the caller named one.

vip_release.description: The INSTALLED VIP's own version/release-notes/feature-matrix facts, discovered by a real filesystem scan of $DESIGNWARE_HOME (dv_harness/env_manifest.py's scan_designware_home()). This answers 'which VIP release is this environment actually built against' from the install tree itself rather than from a version number someone typed into a document -- the same reasoning that makes the zero-time config dump above more trustworthy than a user guide. Nothing here is read INTO the manifest as content: release notes and feature matrices are recorded as path + sha256 + byte size only (see release_notes/feature_matrix below), never inlined.

status.description: SCANNED: a real DESIGNWARE_HOME directory was walked and `packages` reflects what was genuinely found there (which may legitimately be an empty array if the tree contains no recognisable VIP package). NOT_AVAILABLE: DESIGNWARE_HOME was unset, or was set to a path that does not exist -- distinguished by `reason`.

designware_home.description: The real DESIGNWARE_HOME value this scan used, echoed back so a manifest generated against the wrong install is diagnosable. Null when unset.

packages.description: One entry per installed VIP package/version directory actually found on disk, sorted by (name, version) for a stable diff.

name.description: VIP package directory name as it really appears in the install tree, e.g. 'usb_svt'.

version.description: Version directory name exactly as installed, e.g. 'R-2020.12'. Null when the package directory has no version level -- never a guessed version.

install_path.description: Real absolute path of the version directory that was scanned.

user_guide_refs.description: POINTERS to VIP user guides that were distilled OFFLINE by dv_harness/vip_user_guide_distill.py (`dv-harness vip-user-guide distill`), never the guides themselves. This layer records paths, sha256s, byte sizes, page count, section COUNT and which extractor ran -- and deliberately not section headings and not one word of document prose. That restraint is the requirement, not an optimisation: CLAUDE.md's Context Budget makes env.manifest.json a TIER-2 ALWAYS-RESIDENT artifact, so anything inlined here is pushed into every session's context window forever, which is exactly what 'distilled offline, never loaded into runtime context' forbids. env_manifest.assert_no_user_guide_body_in_manifest() enforces it as a checkable property.

status.description: INDEXED: at least one real distilled reference record was supplied and read. NOT_AVAILABLE: none was -- `documents` is empty, and no user guide has been distilled for this environment yet.

documents.description: One entry per distilled document, sorted by title for a stable diff.

doc_kind.description: What the document actually is: 'vip_user_guide', 'protocol_spec', 'programming_guide', ... so a reader never has to guess which document a pointer refers to.

distilled_reference.description: The bounded tier-3 navigation index (.reference.md) -- read on demand, never preloaded.

full_text_extract.description: The complete extracted plain text: the TARGETED-READ target, never a context load.

method.description: Which extraction really ran. 'pre_extracted_text' means someone handed us a .txt -- page numbers are honestly absent for that path rather than invented.

section_count.description: How many numbered headings the distiller detected. A COUNT, not the headings -- the headings live in the .reference.md this entry points at.

status.description: CAPTURED: vip_instances below was parsed from a real dump file a live UVM simv actually produced. NOT_AVAILABLE: no such dump exists yet for this environment -- vip_instances is an empty array, never fabricated example content.

reason.description: Required explanation when status=NOT_AVAILABLE (e.g. 'no live simv exists yet for this environment'); null when CAPTURED.

vip_instances.description: One entry per VIP config object the dump's end_of_elaboration_phase callback registered. Empty when status=NOT_AVAILABLE.

instance_path.description: Full hierarchical path of the VIP config object, exactly as get_full_name() reported it at dump time.

vip_type.description: The VIP config class's own get_type_name().

config_fields.description: Field name -> stringified resolved value, exactly as the VIP's own config object reported them (never re-derived from documentation).

address_map.description: Decoded address regions, read from a soc_arch_map.schema.json input file produced by the project's own SoC spec pipeline. Each entry additionally carries a register_map_agreement cross-check computed against dut_facts.registers -- the two fact sources describe overlapping reality, and silently trusting whichever was loaded last is exactly the failure CLAUDE.md's Source Authority Order exists to prevent.

entries.description: Passthrough of the input's own `address_map` entries, sorted by base_address then name for a stable diff, each with register_map_agreement added.

register_map_agreement.description: AGREES: a register-map block of the same name declares the same base address (compared as integers, so 0x1000 and 0x01000 agree). DISAGREES: same name, different base -- a real conflict for a human to resolve, never auto-resolved here. NOT_IN_REGISTER_MAP: the register map was loaded and has no block of this name, which is normal for a region with no software-visible registers. NOT_AVAILABLE: no register map was loaded at all, so no cross-check was possible -- deliberately distinct from NOT_IN_REGISTER_MAP, since 'nothing to compare against' is not the same finding as 'compared, and absent'.

disagreement_count.description: How many entries came back DISAGREES. Present so a consumer can act on the conflict without walking the array.

clock_reset.description: Clock-domain and reset topology from the same soc_arch_map.schema.json input. Reset `active_level` is required by that input contract and carried verbatim here: an assumed reset polarity is one of the cheapest ways to hold a DUT in reset for a whole run while every machine gate still reports PASS.

clocks.description: Sorted by name for a stable diff.

resets.description: Sorted by name for a stable diff.

clock_resolved.description: RESOLVED: this reset's `clock` names a clock that really appears in `clocks`. UNKNOWN_CLOCK: it names one that does not -- a real inconsistency in the input, surfaced rather than carried silently. NOT_SPECIFIED: the input gave no clock for this reset.

reason.description: Required explanation when status=NOT_AVAILABLE (e.g. no rtl_files supplied); null when PARSED.

files.description: One entry per RTL source file, sorted by file_path for a stable diff. Each entry is verible_parser.to_dict()'s own real, unmodified shape.

instances.description: Module instantiations inside this module's body, with their port connections. Added 2026-09-04 alongside verible_parser.py's instantiation extraction: this is the structural wiring a port-level connectivity graph is built from (dv_harness/amba_fabric_discovery.py's AMBA-7..14 endpoint tracing), which a declaration-only view cannot express. NOT in `required`, so a manifest written before that extraction existed still validates rather than being forced through a version bump for an additive fact.

port_name.description: null for a POSITIONAL connection -- resolving which formal port that slot names needs the instantiated module's own port list, which is a different file's fact.

position.description: 0-based slot in the port-actual list, counted from the comma separators (verible elides an omitted positional slot entirely).

nets.description: Base identifiers the connected expression references -- what a net-level graph joins on. Empty for an explicitly-unconnected port or a constant.

continuous_assigns.description: Continuous `assign` statements in this module's body. AMBA-7 requires a trace to cross wire assignments and aliases; a 1:1 lhs/rhs pair is exactly such an alias. Added 2026-09-04, non-required for the same backward-compatibility reason as `instances`.

status.description: LOADED: blocks below was read from a real register-map JSON file conforming to register_map.schema.json (dv_harness/schemas/register_map.schema.json is the input contract -- a RAL/IP-XACT export, never hand-invented content). NOT_AVAILABLE: no register-map input was supplied for this environment.

blocks.description: Passthrough of the register-map input's own `blocks` array, unmodified. Empty when status=NOT_AVAILABLE. See register_map.schema.json for the item shape -- deliberately not re-declared here so the two schemas cannot drift apart silently.

testplan_correspondence.description: The computed three-way correspondence between the TESTLIST (what regression runs), the VPLAN ITEMS (what verification claims to verify, and which tests/coverage each claims), and the COVERAGE MODEL (what covergroups/coverpoints/assertions actually exist in written SV). Input contract: dv_harness/schemas/testplan_sources.schema.json. env_manifest.py never invents any of the three lists -- it JOINS them, which is the point: each list read alone always looks healthy, and only the join exposes a vPlan item claiming a test nobody runs, a covergroup no vPlan item references, or a regression test that maps to no stated verification intent. Matching is a literal name join, never fuzzy -- a fuzzy match would manufacture correspondence that does not exist.

status.description: COMPUTED: all three axes were supplied and fully joined. PARTIAL: at least one axis was supplied but not all three -- the checks that need a missing axis are honestly skipped (their per-item verdicts read NOT_CHECKED) rather than being scored as passing against nothing. NOT_AVAILABLE: no testplan-sources input was supplied at all.

axes_available.description: Which of the three axes the input actually carried. This is what makes PARTIAL actionable -- 'incomplete' is useless without naming the missing side.

items.description: One entry per vPlan item, sorted by id for a stable diff. Empty when no vplan_items axis was supplied.

tests_present.description: Claimed test names that really exist in the testlist.

tests_missing.description: Claimed test names that exist in NO testlist entry -- a vPlan item claiming coverage from a test nobody runs.

coverage_missing.description: Claimed coverage names that exist in NO coverage-model entry -- a vPlan item measured by a covergroup nobody wrote.

verdict.description: LINKED: every claim this item makes resolves against a real test/coverage entry. BROKEN_*_REF: at least one claim resolves against nothing. UNCLAIMED: the item claims no tests and no coverage at all -- verification intent with nothing attached to it, which a per-axis check alone can never surface. NOT_CHECKED: neither the testlist nor the coverage-model axis was supplied, so this item's claims could not be checked against anything and are deliberately NOT reported as LINKED.

orphans.description: The reverse direction, which the per-item join above cannot see.

tests_not_in_any_vplan_item.description: Tests the regression really runs that no vPlan item claims -- simulation time spent against no stated verification intent. Empty (not omitted) when both axes were supplied and there are none.

coverage_not_referenced_by_any_vplan_ite.description: Coverage constructs that really exist in SV but that no vPlan item references -- coverage being collected against no stated intent.

status.description: CAPTURED: components below was parsed from a real hierarchy dump a live UVM run's end_of_elaboration_phase actually produced (walking uvm_top's real children -- see templates/uvm_env_manifest/dv_env_manifest_pkg.sv). NOT_AVAILABLE: no such dump exists yet.

is_active.description: get_is_active() for a uvm_agent-derived component; NOT_APPLICABLE for a component with no active/passive concept -- an agent asking whether a component is active or passive reads this field instead of guessing from the component's name.

status.description: CAPTURED: entries below was extracted from a real sim log produced by a run with +UVM_CONFIG_DB_TRACE set. NOT_AVAILABLE: no such log was supplied.

parse_confidence.description: Honesty flag on how entries[].message was extracted: the outer UVM_INFO report envelope (file/line/time/reporter/id) is a stable, well-documented format and is fully parsed; the message BODY's own internal field/value sub-format is NOT further decomposed (never verified against a live UVM run in this repo) and is kept as opaque raw text in entries[].message rather than guessed apart into structured sub-fields. Null when status=NOT_AVAILABLE.

kind.description: From the report's own [CFGDB/SET] / [CFGDB/GET] message id.

message.description: Raw, unparsed message body -- see parse_confidence above.

repository_sha_ref.description: One repository's real HEAD commit, or an honest reason it could not be read. 'We could not check' (NOT_AVAILABLE) and 'nobody asked us to check' (NOT_DECLARED) stay distinct, because they are different operator problems with different fixes.

sha.description: Full commit hash exactly as git reported it; null unless RESOLVED. Never truncated and never invented.

doc_file_ref.description: A POINTER to a real file on disk, never its content. Identity (sha256) and size are recorded so a consumer can tell whether the file it finds is the one this manifest described, and so a stale reference is detectable -- but the bytes themselves stay out of this always-resident manifest by construction.

path.description: Real path to the file; null when this particular reference genuinely does not exist (e.g. a VIP package that ships no feature matrix).

sha256.description: Content hash of the real file; null when path is null.

bytes.description: Real byte size; null when path is null.

page_count.description: Pages, for a paginated source document. Null for any non-paginated source -- never a fabricated count.

kind.description: What real artifact this layer was read from, e.g. vip_config_dump_json, register_map_json, topology_dump_json, sim_log_uvm_config_db_trace.

path.description: Path to the real source artifact this layer was extracted from, relative to the environment root; null when status=NOT_AVAILABLE (nothing was read).
